chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who raised it (mursal), saying:

Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said: 'O group of disciples! I have a need from you — fulfil it for me.' They said: 'Your need is fulfilled, O Spirit of God!' So he arose and washed their feet. They said: 'We were more deserving of this (washing your feet), O Spirit of God!'
So he said: 'Indeed the most deserving of people for service is the scholar. I have only humbled myself like this so that you may be humble after me among people, as I have been humble toward you.'
Then Isa (peace be upon him) said: 'Wisdom is cultivated through humility, not through arrogance, and likewise it is in the plain that crops grow, not on the mountain.'

key_terms.التواضع: Humility/modesty (tawadu') — the foundation for cultivating wisdom
key_terms.الحكمة: Wisdom (hikmah) — divine wisdom that encompasses both knowledge and right action
key_terms.الحواريون: The disciples (Hawariyyun) — the close followers and companions of Prophet Isa (AS)
key_terms.العالم: The scholar/learned one (al-'alim) — one who carries and transmits divine knowledge
key_terms.روح الله: Spirit of God (Ruh Allah) — a Quranic title for Prophet Isa (AS), referenced in Quran 4:171

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Isa (Jesus) teach about humility and wisdom in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a narrative account of Prophet Isa (Jesus, peace be upon him) washing the feet of his disciples (Hawariyyun), using this act of service as a lesson in humility. The disciples protested that they should be the ones serving him, to which Isa replied that the scholar is the one most deserving of service — yet humbles himself as an example for others. He then offers the beautiful agricultural metaphor that wisdom, like crops, flourishes in the humble plain, not on the proud mountain. The hadith is mursal (a gap exists in the chain) and is cited in the chapter on the qualities of scholars, establishing humility as a defining virtue of true learning.
